h1: AI UGC Ads Made for YouTube Shorts
lead: Plenty of YouTube ads lose the viewer before the product appears. A YouTube Shorts ad can sound like a creator, open fast, and keep people watching long enough to buy.
card: YouTube Shorts ads from a photo or a product link, in the tall shape Shorts uses.

faq.q: What is an AI YouTube Shorts ad?
faq.a: It is a tall creator-style Short. An [AI actor](/ai-video-generation/ai-actors) can hold the product or give one reason to try it. You pick the language, and you do not wait on a creator.

faq.q: Can a YouTube Shorts ad get people to watch longer?
faq.a: An opening on the product is easier to stay with than a logo. If fewer people skip, you will see that in YouTube. We do not promise a longer watch.

faq.q: What does a YouTube Shorts ad cost?
faq.a: You pay credits for each Short. A video is 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits for 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600.

faq.q: How real do the face and the voice look?
faq.a: The mouth meets the words. The voice can sit in an accent you pick. If YouTube asks you to say the person is AI, say it.

faq.q: Can I change the script, the avatar, and the picture?
faq.a: Yes. Rewrite the line after you see the avatar, swap who holds the product, and download the new Short.

faq.q: Will YouTube accept an AI Short as an ad?
faq.a: It can, if the product in the video is the product you ship and you say so when YouTube asks. We do not publish the ad for you. Read the disclosure rules on the day you post.

faq.q: Does a Short start from a product link?
faq.a: Yes. The product page can start the YouTube Shorts ad, and a product photo can start it too. A wide video that plays before another YouTube video is its own file.

faq.q: Which frame should a Shorts ad use?
faq.a: Use 9:16 for Shorts. A 16:9 file is a separate wide job. Check [social media ad sizes](/guides/ad-sizes-by-platform) before you download.
